newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Opposition says would look at "fair" GST.
newsitem.headline: Australia Opposition says would look at "fair" GST.

text.p: The Australian opposition said on Monday it may support a goods and service tax (GST) if it could be implemented fairly.
However, opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said it seemed impossible to develop an equitable GST that would not discriminate against lower-income earners.

"If the business community, if the welfare community can get together, come up with some proposal that makes some kind of sense on all these fronts ... of course, we'd have a look at any such proposal," Evans told Australian Broadcasting Corp.
"But one hasn't been coming forward so far and it's very difficult to see one emerging."
Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Sunday the government would have to look at reforming the tax system at some stage.

"I wouldn't start getting time specific about that, but there's no doubt that at some stage, we will have to reform the Australian taxation system," Howard said in answer to a question about when the government would look at introducing a GST.

The conservative Liberal-National government promised before the March 1996 election not to introduce a GST, but has since qualified that promise by saying it would not introduce such a tax in its first term.
